title: Set 77

sentences.ko: 내일 재우는 건 네가 해 줄 수 있어? 물 달라고 하면 내가 일어난다는 걸 애가 알아챘거든. 그러고 나면 화장실, 그다음엔 복도 불 켜 달라고 하고, 계속 그런 식으로 이어져. 한 시간 반을 거기 있다가 나왔는데 애보다 내가 더 지쳐 있더라. 매번 일어나 주는 게 나니까 그건 내 탓이지.
sentences.text: Can you do bedtime tomorrow? Because he's figured out that if he asks for water I'll get up, and then it's the bathroom, and then he wants the hallway light on, and it just keeps going like that. I was in there an hour and a half and I came out more tired than he was. And I know I'm the one who keeps getting up, so that's on me.

alts.text: Any chance you can take bedtime tomorrow? He's worked out that if he asks for water I'm gonna get up, and then it's the bathroom, and then he wants the hallway light on, and it just goes and goes. I was in there an hour and a half and came out more wiped than he was. And yeah, I'm the one who keeps getting up, so that one's on me.

Would you be able to handle bedtime tomorrow? He has worked out that if he asks for water I will get up, and then it is the bathroom, and then he wants the hallway light on, and it continues like that. I was in there for an hour and a half and came out more tired than he was. I am aware that I am the one who keeps getting up, so the responsibility is mine.

sentences.note: **figured out** 은 아이가 요령을 터득했다는 뜻입니다. **that's on me** 는 그건 내 탓이라고 스스로 인정할 때 쓰는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 메인가에서 세 군데를 갔는데 어디도 앉을 자리가 없었어. 마지막 집은 줄이 문밖까지 나와 있어서 결국 처음 있던 자리로 도로 돌아왔잖아. 나는 쉬는 날이라 커피는 아무래도 상관없어. 그냥 우리 집 말고 다른 데 좀 앉아 있고 싶었던 거야. 다음엔 아홉 시에 갈까?
sentences.text: We tried three places on Main and there was nowhere to sit in any of them, and the last one had a line out the door, so we ended up right back where we started. And it's my day off, so I don't even care about the coffee, I just wanted to sit somewhere that isn't my apartment. Can we go at nine next time?

alts.text: We hit three places on Main and not one of them had a seat, and the last one had a line out the door, so we wound up right back where we started. And it's my day off, so I don't even care about the coffee, I just wanted to sit somewhere that isn't my apartment. Wanna go at nine next time?

We tried three places on Main and there was no seating available in any of them, and the last one had a line extending out the door, so we ended up exactly where we began. It is my day off, so the coffee is not really the point; I simply wanted to sit somewhere other than my apartment. Could we go at nine next time?

sentences.note: **a line out the door** 는 줄이 가게 문밖까지 늘어섰다는 말입니다. **right back where we started** 는 이것저것 해 봤지만 결국 제자리로 돌아왔다는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 날이 추워지고 나서 난방이 또 자꾸 꺼져요. 낮에는 괜찮은데 아침에 일어날 때쯤이면 방이 얼음장이에요. 11월에 사람 보내 주셨고 그분이 다 고쳤다고 했는데 똑같은 증상이에요. 그분을 다시 불러 주실 수 있어요? 아니면 다른 분을 보내시는 게 나을까요? 어느 쪽이든 목요일에는 집에 있어요.
sentences.text: So the heat's been cutting out again since it got cold, and it's fine during the day, but the bedrooms are freezing by the time we get up. I know you sent somebody out in November and he told us it was fixed, but it's doing the exact same thing. Can you get him back, or should you send someone else? I'm home Thursday either way.

alts.text: The heat keeps cutting out again now that it's cold, and it's fine during the day, but the bedrooms are freezing by the time we're up. You sent somebody out in November and he told us it was fixed, but it's doing the exact same thing. Can you get him back out, or are you sending someone else? I'm home Thursday either way.

The heating has been cutting out again since the cold weather arrived, and it is fine during the day, but the bedrooms are freezing by the time we get up. I understand you sent someone out in November and he told us it had been repaired, but it is doing precisely the same thing. Could you have him return, or would you prefer to send someone else? I am home on Thursday in either case.

sentences.note: **cutting out** 은 기계가 돌아가다가 저절로 멎는 것을 말합니다. **either way** 는 둘 중 어느 쪽으로 하셔도 상관없다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 집주인이랑 고장 난 것 고쳐 달라고 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 내가 일 그만둔 걸 다들 이미 들어서 알고 있더라. 한 시간쯤 사이에 네 사람한테 똑같은 질문을 받았고, 그때마다 처음 얘기하듯이 전부 다시 설명해야 했어. 게다가 엄마가 방 저쪽에서 맞지도 않는 얘기를 자꾸 보태서 그것까지 바로잡고 있었지. 나중에는 십 초짜리로 줄여서 말하고 애들은 잘 크냐고 되물어서 그 자리를 빠져나왔어.
sentences.text: Everybody had already heard I left the job, so I got the same question from four different people in about an hour, and I had to tell the whole thing again every time like it was new. And my mom kept adding stuff from across the room that wasn't even right, so then I'm correcting her too. By the end I was doing the ten second version and asking about their kids just to get out of it.

alts.text: Word had already gotten around that I left the job, so I got the same question from four different people in about an hour, and every time I had to run through the whole thing again like it was news. And my mom kept adding stuff from across the room that wasn't even right, so then I'm fixing that too. By the end I was giving the ten second version and asking about their kids just to get out of it.

Everyone had already heard that I left the job, so I received the same question from four different people within about an hour, and I had to recount the entire story each time as though it were new. My mother kept adding details from across the room that were not even accurate, so I was correcting her as well. By the end I was giving the ten second version and asking after their children simply to escape the conversation.

sentences.note: **the ten second version** 은 길게 말하기 싫을 때 아주 짧게 줄인 이야기를 뜻합니다. **just to get out of it** 은 그 상황에서 벗어나려고 그랬다는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친척들 모인 자리에서 질문 공세 받은 얘기

sentences.ko: 솔직히? 재킷은 예뻐. 근데 네가 맨날 입는 그 회색이랑 너무 비슷해. 그리고 네가 물어봤잖아. 그러니까 마음에 들면 그냥 입어. 내가 말리지는 않을게. 근데 조금이라도 망설여지면 나 같으면 환불하겠어. 회색을 두고 이걸 집어 들 일은 없을 것 같거든.
sentences.text: Honestly? It's a nice jacket, it's just really close to that gray one you wear all the time, and you did ask me. So if you love it, keep it, I'm not going to talk you out of it. But if you're on the fence at all I'd take it back, because I don't think you'd ever grab this one over the gray.

alts.text: You want the truth? It's a nice jacket, it's just really close to that gray one you're always wearing, and hey, you asked me. So if you love it, keep it, I'm not gonna talk you out of it. But if you're even a little unsure I'd take it back, cause I don't think you'd ever reach for this one over the gray.

To be honest, it is a nice jacket. It is simply very similar to the gray one you wear all the time, and you did ask me. So if you love it, keep it; I will not try to talk you out of it. But if you have any hesitation at all, I would return it, because I do not believe you would ever choose this one over the gray.

sentences.note: **on the fence** 는 살까 말까 결정을 못 하고 망설이는 상태입니다. **talk you out of it** 은 하지 말라고 설득해서 마음을 돌린다는 뜻입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 산 옷 어떠냐고 물었을 때 솔직하게 말하기

reviewed: 2번 formal 의 "Might we go at nine next time?" 는 요즘 원어민이 거의 쓰지 않는 옛말투라 "Could we go at nine next time?" 로 고쳤습니다. 격식만 올리면 되지 고어체로 갈 필요는 없습니다.
1번 formal 의 "it continues in that fashion" 은 격식체를 넘어 문어체라 소리내어 말하면 어색합니다. "and it continues like that" 으로 낮췄습니다 — 뜻은 그대로입니다.
5번 casual 의 "that gray one you wear constantly" 에서 constantly 는 캐주얼보다 글에 가까운 낱말이라 "that gray one you're always wearing" 으로 바꿨습니다.
